title: Activity-Based DNA-Encoded Library Technology
text:
The human genome sequence was originally thought to be a user manual for understanding and curing
human diseases, but translating its contents into the testable experiments required to discover new
medicines is tedious, expensive, and sometimes impossible for certain “undruggable” genes. My
laboratory is developing technology that will democratize drug discovery and render it “plug-and-play”
to target any disease-related gene. This new therapeutic strategy is likely to have broad applicability to
the discovery of new antibiotics, antivirals, anti-cancer agents, and cholesterol-lowering drugs to name
a few.

title: Defining the role of IGF2 in regulating adipocyte progenitor proliferation and adipogenesis
text:
Whether obesity is unhealthy depends in large part upon the balance between maladaptive fat expansion via
adipocyte hypertrophy (growth in pre-existing fat cells) and metabolically protective fat expansion via adipocyte
hyperplasia (increasing numbers of new fat cells). In this proposal, we will investigate the potential of insulin-like
growth factor 2 (IGF2) to promote adipocyte progenitor proliferation and differentiation, the dynamic processes
that drive hyperplastic fat expansion. The results of this proposal will provide a better understanding of whether
enhanced IGF2 action in adipocyte progenitors is a viable strategy for promoting hyperplastic fat expansion and
uncoupling obesity from metabolic disease.

title: PopScreen: Implementing Population Genomic Screening in Primary Care
text:
Genomic screening for the general population may save lives and be cost-effective. However, if genomic
screening is to move forward for real-world clinical implementation, it will require participation by primary care
providers, who already provide most preventive care. In this study, we will conduct an implementation trial of
genomic screening for actionable diseases in primary care and establish best practices to ensure the effective
and sustainable future implementation of genomic screening.

title: Role of persistent sodium currents in modulating mosquito sensory behavior
text:
This application describes basic research to understand the role of voltage-gated sodium channels in shaping
the sensory physiology and behavior of human disease-transmitting mosquitoes. The knowledge gained from
this research will provide a platform for screening new mosquito repellents and/or formulating new repellent
mixtures to control insect vectors that transmit devastating human infectious diseases.

title: MCOLGEL - Advanced Biocompatible Material for Dental Pulp Capping Therapy
text:
The development of new biomaterials for Dental Pulp Capping therapy is a top priority in dentistry, crucial for preserving the
health and vitality of compromised pulp. This project aims to develop MCOLGEL, a novel biomaterial that promises to
significantly enhance clinical outcomes by promoting healing with reduced inflammation, chemical irritation, and necrosis, while
simultaneously preventing bacterial infection, promoting tissue regeneration, and ensuring affordability. We have
assembled a team with the relevant technical expertise necessary for the successful development, validation of MCOLGEL.

title: BEAT-HIV: Delaney Collaboratory to Cure HIV-1 Infection by Combination Immunotherapy
text:
The inability of antiretroviral therapy (ART) to clear HIV infection and the observation that a sterilizing cure and/or
stable remission can be achieved by a subset of ART-treated persons has galvanized interest to advance clinical
strategies towards a cure and/or stable remission. Including scientists from 12 institutions and 9 industry
partners, the BEAT-HIV Delaney Collaboratory will seek to develop and test innovative combined
immunotherapy strategies to permanently suppress and/or eradicate HIV in the absence of ART.

title: Recombinant hANGPTL4 and CKD
text:
Recombinant mutated human Angiopoietin-like 4 protein will be investigated for its potential role
in reducing or eliminating the progression of chronic kidney disease in rat and minpig models.
Anti-apoptosis mechanisms that maintain interstitial capillary endothelium integrity and keep
repair vessels open to reduce interstitial fibrosis will be investigated in endothelial Integrin
knockout mouse models.

title: Dissecting the function of Nemp1, a nuclear envelope protein critical for mammalian fertility
text:
RELEVANCE TO PUBLIC HEALTH
A woman's supply of eggs (oocytes), which are present in her ovary from birth, are essential for her fertility, and
for her long-term health, as loss of the oocyte pool leads to menopause, with increase risks of osteoporosis,
cardiovascular disease and muscle atrophy. Mutations in human Nemp1 are associated with early menopause,
and loss of Nemp1 in mouse models leads to infertility. By studying how Nemp1 functions using mouse models,
we can better understand how we can support a woman's fertility and her health, and diagnose some causes of
infertility.

title: The effects of APOE genotype in homeostatic microglial function in preclinical APOE mouse model
text:
Aging and APOE4 genotype are the strongest risk factor for Alzheimer's disease (AD). However, how
these risk factors affect the homeostatic microglial function and responses to amyloid  (A) prior to AD pathology
remains unclear. I will determine the specific mechanism by which APOE4 contributes to these dysregulations
using a targeted replacement APOE mice expressing GFP in microglia by doing whole RNA-seq analysis of
microglia, and studying microglia responses to A ex-vivo, potentially identifying a new AD therapeutic target.

title: Next-Generation Enabling Technologies for Ultrafast Functional Pulmonary MRI
text:
We propose to use next-generation laser-diode arrays to enable more scalable, user-friendly, and cost-effective
production technology for hyperpolarized xenon-129 gas, an emerging new imaging modality for functional
pulmonary imaging. Specifically, new ultra-frequency-narrowed purpose-built lasers will be employed to boost
hyperpolarized xenon-129 production efficiency, with the vision that recent gains in frequency narrowing can
enable efficient contrast agent production with vastly reduced laser power and milder conditions. The new
technology will be fully integrated into a clinical-scale hyperpolarizer and available to the end users by the end
of the project.

title: Unraveling the functional diversity of B cells in health and disease
text:
This proposal aims to develop novel algorithms to better characterize the full spectrum of molecular,
cellular, and phenotypic changes that occur in B cells using single cell RNAseq and spatial
transcriptomics data.

title: Multiphoton In Vivo Microscopy (Core 2)
text: Discovering the basic molecular and cellular mechanisms of post-traumatic epileptogenesis in a biophysically realistic model of traumatic brain injury will require having longitudinal, high-resolution access to the gyrencephalic, large animal brain. Fluorescence microscopy enhances such capabilities, enabling multimodal data collection through the use of genetically targeted and ion-selective fluorophores. In the tool development Phase I of this project, we developed an instrument and supporting technologies that afford us the unique ability to perform such measurements. These technologies include a custom two-photon microscope with a gantry design that can accommodate imaging in vivo, with subcellular resolution, brains of animals weighing >80kg. Microscopic in vivo imaging in animals of this size (to our knowledge, the largest by a factor of 2-4x) required substantial development and optimization of motion artifact mitigation tools, including heartbeat-triggered, high speed image stack acquisition; flexible, penetrable, transparent sub-dural windows; and post-hoc image registration algorithms. Finally, the microscope can perform digital fluorescence lifetime imaging, enabling quantification of extracellular chloride using novel single-wavelength dyes. The Microscopy Core will implement the imaging tools developed in Phase I, as well as optimize for calcium imaging and long-term repeated access. As these tools require substantial cost and technical expertise, the Microscopy Core represents a cost-effective consolidation and consistent implementation for the proposed program.

title: Precision imaging of electromechanical coupling for non-invasive cardiac arrhythmia mapping
text:
Atrial and ventricular cardiac arrhythmias, are serious public health problems in the United States, affecting over
5% of Americans and are major causes of stroke and heart failure leading to increased morbidity and mortality.
This proposed preclinical study and clinical trial will determine how electromechanical wave imaging, a non-
invasive ultrasound precision imaging modality can effectively diagnose and determine the mechanism of the
arrhythmia and impact personalized treatment of cardiac arrhythmias.

title: Foundation Models for Human Functional Neuroimaging with Applications to Psychiatric Disorders
text:
In response to the NIMH Notice of Special Interest (NOT-MH-21-175), this project aims to harness large-scale
data and develop and apply cutting-edge Artificial Intelligence techniques to advance our understanding of the
complex neurobiology underlying highly prevalent psychiatric disorders. We will analyze large-scale human
brain imaging and phenotypic data from the Human Connectome Project and related datasets to identify
personalized neurobiological markers and predict symptom severity across multiple conditions. By creating
powerful and adaptable computational tools, this research will lay the groundwork for more precise diagnostic
and treatment strategies, potentially transforming mental healthcare outcomes.

title: Multimode High-Throughput Screening Microplate Reader
text:
The PHERAstar FSX microplate reader will allow researchers at the U-M to perform HTS in order to
identify novel drug candidates by testing the interaction of thousands of compounds. With this state-of-the-art
microplate reader, researchers can quickly prioritize which compounds might be successful in treating
diseases, such as cardiovascular disease, cancer, diabetes, and infectious diseases. By expediting the
identification of candidate compounds, HTS accelerates the drug discovery process and directly influences
available treatments for disease.

title: MR Image-Guided Drug Delivery to Cerebral Cavernous Malformations with Focused Ultrasound
text:
Cerebral cavernous malformations (CCMs) are vascular lesions in the central nervous system that cause
debilitating neurological problems. CCMs are usually treated by surgical removal, which is invasive and risky. In
this proposal, we are developing and testing an MR image-guided technology (i.e. focused ultrasound) for
overcoming physical barriers to drug delivery to CCMs in an effort to better control their pathological progression.

title: Housing assistance, Outcomes, Medicare, and SEER (HOMES): using a novel data linkage to understand cancer inequities
text:
Safe and affordable housing provides a critical foundation for health; however, its relationship with cancer care
and outcomes is largely unknown. This study examines whether patients with cancer who receive federal
housing assistance are more likely to receive timely, guideline-concordant care for breast, colorectal, prostate,
and lung cancers compared to similar patients without housing assistance.

title: Analytic Core C
text: PROJECT SUMMARY – ANALYTIC CORE The mission of the Perimenopause in Brain Aging and Alzheimer’s Disease Program Project (P3) is to define the biological transformations that occur during the perimenopausal transition and increase vulnerability to AD in postmenopausal women. Here we focus on the impact of menopause hormone therapy (MHT) on the female aging brain and address the critical question of why the timing of MHT initiation yields divergent outcomes on AD risk. By elucidating the mechanisms that drive differential responsiveness to MHT across ApoE genotypes and perimenopausal stages, our overarching goal is to establish the mechanistic and translational foundation for precision, stratified use of MHT to prevent or delay the progression to an AD at-risk phenotype. Analytic Core advances the goals of the Perimenopause Program Project by providing centralized specimen management, standardized sample processing, and streamlined analytic and bioinformatic support to individual Projects and Cores to maximize reproducibility. To achieve this mission, Analytic Core operates across three coordinated levels of support. The first layer focuses on standardized sample processing, quality control, metadata capture, and long-term sample banking and management. The second layer involves conducting key analyses, including steroid hormone assessment, bulk tissue and cell RNA sequencing, single-cell and single-nucleus RNA sequencing, and spatial transcriptomics. The third layer provides robust bioinformatic support, including -omics data processing and analysis. Individual “omics” datasets generated by the Analytic Core will also be provided to the Administrative Core to enable integrated multi-omics analyses across the Program Project. By providing comprehensive analytical and informatic support, the Analytic Core will remain integral to achieving the overall mission and specific aims of the Program Project.

title: Developing next-generation mass spectrometric platforms for molecular cartography of the cellular membranes
text:
This project develops advanced mass spectrometry-based technologies to directly analyze membrane protein
complexes and their surrounding lipid environments within native and reconstituted membranes. By integrating
native MS, lipidomics, and polymer-based native nanodisc platforms, we will uncover how membrane
composition and organization influence protein assemblies that regulate key cellular functions. These efforts will
provide critical insights into membrane-associated signaling mechanisms and their dysregulation in disease,
ultimately advancing biomedical research and therapeutic discovery.

title: SimulScan: Simultaneous functional and dynamic MRI for evaluating swallowing across age and in neurogenic dysphagia
text:
Dysphagia, or difficulty swallowing, is a common symptom of many neurological diseases but remains
poorly understood. In this project, we optimize a multimodal imaging tool using magnetic resonance
imaging to provide the unprecedented measurement of both the dynamic motions associated with
swallowing, along with the associated neural activity to enhance understanding of swallowing control.
This tool will be validated in healthy adults and a sample of patients with neurogenic dysphagia in an
effort to improve neurogenic dysphagia characterization and help improve diagnosis and management
of this debilitating health condition in the future.
